data.title: Oosterhuis: A giant of game with a sweet 2-iron
data.description: It was a filthy day with non-stop rain pounding the Hilversumsche course and I found myself sitting on a clubhouse couch next to Peter Oosterhuis. Back in 1974, Peter was the man of the moment and was consistently winning tournaments over a ten-year period. We chatted about this and that and he mentioned he was hoping to go out and play, as he was only one shot back. All the other players, who were not in contention, didn't want to go out in the Dutch monsoon. However, the tournament ultimately was reduced to just three rounds and Brian Barnes was declared the winner.

data.title: Comfort vs desire
data.description: Prime Video's A Love Other Than Yours explores the changing emotions of a long-term relationship through four characters searching for love, understanding and connection.

data.title: Quebec's incoming separatist leader wants to block Crown from swearing-in
data.description: MONTREAL (CANADA) - Quebec's incoming separatist premier said Tuesday he plans to block the province's lieutenant governor, a representative of the British Crown, from swearing in the new government.

data.title: Iceland is 'critical outpost' for security, says Rubio during visit
data.description: REYKJAVIK - US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Tuesday that Iceland had long been a "critical outpost" for security during a visit to the island, as his country pushes for greater American influence in the Arctic region.

data.title: Thunder Castle open  Shopee Cup defence
data.description: Defending champions Buriram United will kick off their Asean Club Championship Shopee Cup campaign in Group A, taking on Indonesia's Borneo Samarinda on Wednesday.

data.title: Ten-man Thailand fall short
data.description: Thailand came within one penalty of a remarkable triumph in Jakarta on Monday night as Emil Audero saved Nattapong Sayriya's spot-kick to give Indonesia a 4-2 shootout victory and the inaugural Fifa Asean Cup.

data.title: Powerlifter Kamolpan eyes medal
data.description: Powerlifter Kamolpan Kraratpet, Thailand's sole medallist in the discipline, at the last Asian Para Games, will lead a six-strong team to Japan this month in search of a place on the podium again.

data.title: 2,000 swine drown at flooded farm
data.description: Authorities expect to clear about 2,000 pig carcasses from a flooded farm in Prachin Buri by Thursday, Agriculture and Cooperatives Minister Suriya Juangroongruangkit said.

data.title: Higher VAT urged amid net deficit
data.description: The government has reported a net deficit of 760 billion baht for fiscal 2025, as senators called for a higher value-added tax (VAT) and a broader tax base.

data.title: BMA steps up efforts to drain flooded communities
data.description: The Bangkok Metropolitan Administration (BMA) is accelerating floodwater drainage operations at Rom Klao Community Housing in Lat Krabang district.

data.title: BJT gives its MP benefit of the doubt
data.description: Digital Economy and Society Minister Chaichanok Chidchob has defended Bhumjaithai Party MP Suchada Zhang Thaensap, saying he has seen no evidence linking her husband to scam networks.

data.title: Tribute paid to Oct 6 Thammasat tragedy
data.description: Thailand's democracy "has never been fully fledged", said opposition leader Natthaphong Ruengpanyawut at an event marking the 50th anniversary of the Oct 6, 1976 massacre.

data.title: Opposition set to file censure bid
data.description: People's Party leader Natthaphong Ruengpanyawut said on Tuesday the opposition would soon submit a no-confidence motion, with the debate expected by late October or early next month.

data.title: NHRC raises concerns over public broadcaster funding
data.description: The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) has expressed concern that proposed legislation to alter the funding sources of four public organisations could undermine media independence and affect fundamental public rights and freedoms.

data.title: Hospitals told to stock seven days of medicines
data.description: The Ministry of Public Health has ordered hospitals to stockpile enough medicines for at least seven days and food for 10 days ahead of more rain in the South next week.

data.title: Mother, daughters found dead after loan scam
data.description: A single mother and her two young daughters were found dead in their rented home in Pathum Thani on Tuesday after she was allegedly duped in a fraudulent loan application.

data.title: Families allege scam over taekwondo training fees
data.description: CHAIYAPHUM: Four families have asked police and the Sports Authority of Thailand (SAT) to investigate a taekwondo coach in Muang district after claiming they were ripped off.

data.title: Deluge pushes up vegetable, egg prices
data.description: Widespread flooding has disrupted agricultural production in several parts of Thailand, reducing supplies and pushing up vegetable and egg prices, Commerce Minister Suphajee Suthumpun said.

data.title: Care home claims spark probe
data.description: The Public Health Ministry has launched an investigation into an elderly care home in Kanchanaburi's Tha Muang district following reports that residents were subjected to physical and psychological abuse and inhumane living conditions.

data.title: Eastern flooding persists
data.description: Flooding in eastern Thailand entered its seventh consecutive day, with stagnant water causing foul odours in some areas.

data.title: Ronaldo opens door for Portugal return, apologises for walkout
data.description: BARCELONA - Cristiano Ronaldo opened the door for a return to the Portuguese national team on Tuesday and apologised for his walkout, while also accusing coach Jorge Jesus of twice breaking his word.

data.title: No signs of plague in Thailand
data.description: Thailand is closely monitoring a suspected plague case in Russia but has found no indication that the disease has entered the country, Public Health Minister Pattana Promphat said.

data.title: 'Nobody seems to care': Russian city shrugs off plague reports
data.description: IRKUTSK (RUSSIA) - Reports of a plague laboratory worker's death in Siberia have caused waves of speculation outside Russia, but in the city where she worked, many appeared unfazed.

data.title: Trump blames France unrest on Islam, migration
data.description: WASHINGTON (UNITED STATES) - US President Donald Trump on Tuesday blamed France's mass student protests on Islam and migration, pushing his global right-wing narrative ahead of tough midterm elections at home.

data.title: Four Indonesian seamen return home after Somali pirate ordeal
data.description: TANGERANG (INDONESIA) - Four Indonesian seamen who were kidnapped and held hostage by Somali pirates aboard an oil tanker for more than five months arrived back home on Tuesday, an AFP reporter saw.

data.title: Israeli settlers beat AFP photographer covering West Bank
data.description: AQRABA (PALESTINIAN TERRITORIES) - Israeli settlers on Tuesday beat an AFP photographer and fired guns in the direction of him and a colleague as they covered ongoing violence by settlers against West Bank olive farmers.

data.title: Germany arrests ex-spy chief on suspicion of giving secrets to foreign powers
data.description: BERLIN - A former German spy chief was arrested Tuesday on suspicion of passing sensitive information to foreign powers, an embarrassing case that comes as the country is seeking to bolster its intelligence agencies.

data.title: IMF warns cost-of-living shocks cause 'lasting deterioration' in affordability
data.description: WASHINGTON (UNITED STATES) - The International Monetary Fund warned Tuesday that price increases for necessities like food and energy, fuelled by the wars in Iran and Ukraine, were more persistent than previously expected.

data.title: World Bank forecasts modest growth for Latin America, highlights climate risks
data.description: WASHINGTON (UNITED STATES) - The World Bank on Tuesday forecast modest economic growth in Latin America and the Caribbean, warning that risks from high energy prices and the climate phenomenon El Nino could impact the region.

data.title: Nómada fires up first Friday with feast and fiesta
data.description: Nómada Open Fire Grill & Beach Club at Dusit Thani Hua Hin just launched 'Nómada Fiesta', a new monthly dining experience bringing together the bold flavours, lively rhythms and warm, convivial spirit of South America.

data.title: Nobel physics prize honours work on 'ghostly messengers' from outer space
data.description: STOCKHOLM - Belgian physicist Francis Halzen on Tuesday won the Nobel physics prize for groundbreaking work using South Pole ice to capture particles originating in the distant cosmos, providing insight into the far reaches of space.

data.title: Bulgaria searches for missing crew after drones hit two more ships in Black Sea
data.description: SOFIA (BULGARIA) - Bulgarian authorities launched a major search on Tuesday for the missing crew of a ship that sank in the Black Sea after drones hit two vessels in what the prime minister slammed as an "absolutely unacceptable" attack.

data.title: Kenya reports first-ever Ebola death
data.description: NAIROBI - Kenya has reported its first-ever Ebola death, the health minister announced on Tuesday, after a Kenyan man who had been living in the Democratic Republic of Congo died after returning to the country.

data.title: Myanmar leader to visit Malaysia after migrant returns begin
data.description: KUALA LUMPUR - Myanmar's coup leader turned president Min Aung Hlaing will head to Malaysia on Wednesday for a two-day visit, officials said, following Kuala Lumpur's plan to return thousands of Myanmar immigrants.

data.title: Germany's AfD poised to preside over state assembly for first time
data.description: MAGDEBURG (GERMANY) - The far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) prepared Tuesday to preside over a state assembly for the first time following its landslide election victory in the eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt.

data.title: Le Pen vows drastic cost savings to prevent French 'default'
data.description: PARIS (FRANCE) - French far-right presidential candidate Marine Le Pen said Tuesday that she would implement 140 billion euros (US$157 billion) in cost savings by 2032 if elected next year, warning that without change France was "heading towards default" on its debt.

data.title: Lisa’s LLOUD launches Von Dutch Hollywood’s first collaboration online Oct 6
data.description: Lisa’s LLOUD collection marks Von Dutch Hollywood’s first collaboration, following its debut at ComplexCon in Los Angeles on October 3–4.

data.title: The Royal Oak is now a necklace
data.description: Audemars Piguet reinterprets the iconic Royal Oak signature band in a high jewellery collection adorned with diamonds and precious stones, bringing together the worlds of horology and haute joaillerie.

data.title: Nene Royal makes voice-acting debut in Disney's 'Hexed'
data.description: Nene Royal, the 16-year-old Thai rocker who won America's Got Talent 2026, will make her acting debut as the Thai voice of Billie Doe, the lead character in Disney's Hexed.
